title: Rav Pappa bar Abba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He lived in the time of Rav Pappa, as in Yevamot 21b, where Rav Pappa said, "For example, the daughter-in-law of the house of Rav Pappa bar Abba." And there, 46a: Rav Pappa said to Rava, "See, sir, these of the house of Pappa bar Abba," etc.

And in Bava Metzia 91a: Rav Pappa said, "These matters were asked of me by those of the house of Rav Pappa bar Abba." And this Rav Pappa bar Abba was corpulent, as in Bava Kamma 10b, where Rav Pappa said, "For example, Pappa bar Abba" (who was corpulent, Rashi). Hyman says Yuchasin was correct in writing that what is said in Bava Metzia 84a, "Rav Pappa himself, like the baskets made in Harpanya," refers to Rav Pappa bar Abba.

And in Seder HaDorot he cites that Rav Pappa bar Abba met Rabbah bar Shmuel and said to him, "Does the master teach anything about the hired worker?" in Bava Metzia — end of quote. The same reading appears in the Iggeret of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 1, ch. 6. Hyman says this is a printer's error and should read Shevuot 45b; there, however, it is Rav Sheshet who met Rabbah bar Shmuel. The error is likewise cited in the entry Rabbah bar Shmuel.
And he had sons who were Torah scholars, as in Shabbat 117a: the sons of Rav Pappa bar Abba said to Rav Pappa; and in Yoma 66b they posed a difficulty to Ravina.

notes.text: Rashi explains dikurei de-Harpanai as baskets made in Harpanya. Hyman attributes this description of corpulence to Pappa bar Abba, distinguishing him from the contemporary Rav Pappa.
Hyman corrects the locator to Shevuot45b and then notes that the passage names Rav Sheshet.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b explicitly calls Pappa bar Abba corpulent, and Rashi on Bava Metzia 84a explains the baskets made in Harpanya. Applying the latter passage’s Pappa description to Pappa bar Abba remains Hyman’s and Yuchasin’s identification. The inspected Shevuot 45b directly names Rav Sheshet meeting Rabbah bar Shmuel; the reported Seder HaDorot and Epistle printing error remains Hyman’s report, not newly inspected print history.
